meta.preheader: NIFTY 50 rose 0.84% to 25,255.05 on Wednesday as banks and autos gained; foreign investors bought ₹12,563 crore (provisional); India's October inflation is due today.
meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Thu 12 Nov: NIFTY 50 rises 0.84% to 25,255.05 as banks and autos lead; October inflation due

brief: In the first session after the Diwali holiday, the NIFTY 50 rose 0.84% to 25,255.05 and the Sensex 0.95% to 81,879.40, after touching a nine-month high of 82,520.40 during the day (Angel One, HDFC Sky, Upstox News).

Nifty Bank gained 1.76% as PSU banks rose 2.94% and autos 2.14%, while IT, realty and pharma fell; the NIFTY Smallcap 100 added 1.59% and advancing shares outnumbered declining ones about two to one on NSE (Upstox News, Liquide).

Foreign investors bought a net ₹12,563 crore and domestic institutions sold ₹8,435 crore (provisional, Trendlyne). The rupee closed 6 paise firmer at 93.71 per dollar (PTI), and the 10-year G-Sec yield rose 6 basis points to 7.21% (Business Standard).

Overseas, US shares rebounded as chipmakers rose, Brent settled 1.4% higher at $92.76 and markets fully priced a December Fed rate rise (Yahoo Finance, Reuters). India's October retail inflation is due today.

drivers.title: Inflation in India
drivers.text: October retail inflation is due today. ICRA's Aditi Nayar expects 6.1% (NewsBytes) and Bank of Baroda's economists about 6%, citing food prices (Devdiscourse); September's reading was 5.54%. Inflation readings shape rate expectations, which reach bond yields and loan rates.

drivers.title: Foreign flows
drivers.text: Foreign investors bought a net ₹65,735 crore in the cash market from 1 to 11 Nov while domestic institutions sold ₹40,504 crore (provisional, Kotak Neo). Foreign flows feed into large-cap share prices and the rupee; provisional figures can be revised.

drivers.title: Crude oil
drivers.text: Brent settled at $92.76 on Wednesday, up $1.27, after Iran said its enriched nuclear material would stay in the country (Reuters); it had fallen to a two-month low on Tuesday. India imports most of its crude, so oil prices reach the import bill, the rupee and fuel inflation.

drivers.title: The rupee and bonds
drivers.text: The rupee firmed 6 paise to 93.71 on Wednesday on foreign inflows and crude near a two-month low during Indian trading (PTI); Brent rose later in the day. The 10-year yield rose 6 basis points to 7.21% as US Treasury yields climbed, with a ₹34,000 crore government bond auction due on Friday (Business Standard, Reuters). Bond prices fall when yields rise.

global_cues.title: US inflation and the Fed
global_cues.text: After October's US consumer prices rose 0.4% against the 0.3% forecast cited by Reuters, markets fully priced a quarter-point Fed rate rise in December; Goldman Sachs and Deutsche Bank now expect rises starting in December (Reuters). Higher US rates can weigh on foreign flows into Indian shares and bonds.

global_cues.title: US yields and the dollar
global_cues.text: The US cash Treasury market was shut on Wednesday for Veterans Day; the 10-year yield had closed at 4.98% on Tuesday (CappNotes). The dollar firmed on Wednesday (Reuters), and a firmer dollar tends to weigh on the rupee and other emerging-market currencies.

global_cues.title: Asian markets
global_cues.text: On Wednesday, Japan's Nikkei rose 1.3% (AP). On Thursday morning Korea's Kospi opened slightly higher, then moved between small gains and losses (Aju Press).

events.title: December Fed rate rise priced in
events.text: October US consumer prices rose 0.4% against the 0.3% forecast cited by Reuters, and markets fully price a December rise; Goldman Sachs expects rises in December and March, Deutsche Bank in December, January and March (Reuters). The channel to India: the dollar, the rupee and foreign flows.

events.title: Iran keeps enriched material at home
events.text: Iran's security council secretary said enriched nuclear material will not leave the country, and Brent rose 1.4% from two-month lows (Reuters). The channel to India: crude prices and the import bill.

events.title: Shipping in the Strait of Hormuz
events.text: Thirty-seven ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz in October, while Middle East supply outages have eased to about 3.8 million barrels a day (Reuters). The channel to India: oil supply and freight costs.

commentary.text: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October against the 0.3% forecast cited by Reuters, and hawkish remarks from Fed officials pushed CME FedWatch odds of a December rise to 100%, which weighs on gold, which pays no interest (Reuters).
Gold gave up an early rebound as the dollar rose to its highest level since April 2025 (Trading Economics), while silver rose about 3% in early trade (Reuters).
ANZ's Soni Kumari said the near-term macro setup for gold does not look positive (Reuters).

stories.headline: Foreign investors added IT and telecom shares in late October while selling financials
stories.what: NSDL data for 16 to 31 October showed net foreign portfolio inflows of ₹10,915 crore into IT and ₹11,065 crore into telecom, while financial services saw ₹883 crore of net outflows in the fortnight and ₹9,517 crore for the month, Kotak Neo reported. Across all sectors, October's net foreign flow was −₹34,843 crore.
stories.why: Sector-level foreign flows show which index weights foreign money is adding or cutting, which feeds into moves in the IT, telecom and financial services indices.

highlights.text: Among equity categories, large and mid cap funds took the most, ₹8,484 crore net, followed by small cap ₹6,407 crore, flexi cap ₹4,980 crore and mid cap ₹4,893 crore; ELSS funds saw a net outflow of ₹578 crore.

Debt funds took a net ₹1,13,438 crore after September's outflows, led by liquid funds (₹70,534 crore) and overnight funds (₹54,893 crore). Total net inflows across all funds were about ₹1.74 lakh crore.
Equity fund assets fell 1.1% to ₹37.15 lakh crore, which AMFI attributed to mark-to-market losses; gold ETFs took ₹3,474 crore and silver ETFs ₹3,092 crore.
Investors added about 15.80 lakh folios in October, taking the total to 28.78 crore.

category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's categorisation rules, a large and mid cap fund must keep at least 35% of its assets in large cap companies and at least 35% in mid cap companies. Large caps are the 100 largest companies by full market value and mid caps those ranked 101 to 250, so at least about a third of the portfolio always sits in mid-sized companies, whose share prices have tended to swing more than those of the largest companies. Each scheme's riskometer level is set out in the fund house's own documents.

learn.title: Why total fund flows can jump while equity flows dip
paragraphs: AMFI's monthly data reports net flows for each category, and the total adds them all up, including money parked for days or weeks.

In October, equity funds took in ₹32,994 crore, less than in September, yet total net inflows were about ₹1.74 lakh crore, because liquid and overnight funds alone took about ₹1.25 lakh crore (AMFI). Companies and institutions often use these funds for short-term cash.
So a large total does not by itself say where long-term investors are putting money; the category lines in AMFI's note show that.
